properties.name: A reply carries its payload once, on every tool, and the per-client shape reaches the six it never reached
properties.rationale: THE CAUSE WAS THE SCOPE OF THE CHECK, NOT THE HELPER. tests/reply_is_sent_once.rs has owned this invariant since 2026-08-23 and asks it of detect_gaps alone, in a crate that already enumerates the served surface for a dozen other properties. So a second reply builder could sit in another module, keep the pre-2026-08-23 shape, and stay green for 28 days. Fixing only the helper would have stopped today's six and left the next builder free to drift the same way, which is why the gate is the substance of this change and the one-line delegation is the smaller half. The helper's own doc-comment was the tell: it asserted "Same shape every other tool returns", which was true when written and silently became false, and nothing reads a comment. A SECOND COST, LARGER THAN THE BYTES: content_policy::apply rewrites a reply only when it is already in signpost shape, so the per-client rule was inert on exactly those six. OpenCode's empty-block fallback, the one it fills from structuredContent itself, never fired on the tools carrying the instructions and the skills; Grok was served correctly by accident. All three measured clients now get the shape they were meant to. WHAT WAS DROPPED AND WHY: the gate does not assert the signpost is smaller than the payload. That assertion is correct on detect_gaps and false across the surface, because the signpost is one fixed sentence and several replies are shorter than it; seven tools failed on it with nothing wrong. Keeping it would have required a size threshold, and this project has twice recorded that a loud detector needs a different question rather than a tuned number. The question that generalises is whether the payload was sent twice, and the gate asks that directly.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: The private `structured` helper in tools/skills_tools.rs now delegates to service::json_result instead of building a second reply shape, so get_instructions, list_skills, get_skill, find_skills, usage_report and design_identity stop sending the payload twice. Measured on the wire before and after, three handshake names: get_instructions went from 64,120 bytes to 32,710 for claude-code and to 31,430 for opencode, and stays at 64,120 for grok-build, which is the per-client rule working rather than being overridden. tools/a_reply_is_sent_once.py is a new CI gate that asks the whole served surface; it was written first and observed to FAIL on exactly those six before the fix. The old one-tool Rust test keeps its three Rust-side assertions and now carries a warning not to mistake it for coverage. AGENTS.md and ci.yml register the gate. REPAIR: corrected_cause — the field is unreachable from add_change_event, so it is stated here in prose.
